newsitem.title: JAPAN: Okinawa angry at U.S. bombs dropped in sea.
newsitem.headline: Okinawa angry at U.S. bombs dropped in sea.

text.p: The governor of the southern Japanese island of Okinawa said on Thursday he was angry about a U.S. Marines jetfighter which jettisoned bombs into the sea off Okinawa.

The Japanese coast guard said on Thursday a U.S. Marines F/A-18 jet dropped the 1,000-lb (450 kg) bomb into the East China Sea on Tuesday about 10 km (6.5 miles) west of the provincial capital of Naha.
The warplane had been conducting bombing exercises on an uninhabited Japanese island in the Pacific, but its bombing device malfunctioned.
Upon approaching the U.S. Air Force base at Kadena, the pilot was ordered to jettison the entire bomb rack into the sea, the coastguard said. The plane landed safely.
The bomb did not explode and the coastguard issued a warning late on Wednesday for inter-island ferry boats to stay away from the area.
"I am suprised and at the same time I am very angry at the fact that this kind of thing happened again," Okinawa Governor Masahide Ota told reporters on Thursday.

After a year of negotiations, Japan and the United States agreed early this month to reduce a fifth of the land taken up by U.S. military facilities on Okinawa, which hosts 75 percent of all U.S. military facilities inside Japan.
The U.S. bases issue flared up last year after the rape of an Okinawan schoolgirl by three U.S. servicemen, who are serving up to 10 years in Japanese prisons.
"This kind of accident will not disappear as long as there are bases," Ota said. "This underlines the importance of our goal to get rid of all U.S. bases on Okinawa."
Ota has demanded the phased withdrawal of all U.S. forces from Okinawa by 2015.
Okinawa is home to about 27,000 U.S. military personnel, including an entire U.S. Marine Corps division. The U.S. Air Force operates Kadena, the largest air base in the western Pacific.
